$schema_note: Service-line taxonomy + unit-to-line mapping (EP-8). DRAFTED BY CLAUDE FOR OWNER REVIEW — every assignment below derives from the unit's `service` string in units.json; `source` quotes that string, `confidence` rates the DERIVATION step (verified = the service string names the line outright; inferred = judgment applied, see note; unverified = no service identity exists to derive from), while the unit's own identity keeps its provenance in units.json. Units whose service is literally 'Unassigned (no public source)' map to line.other with needs_owner_ruling: true — the compiler surfaces these as a warning list, they are NOT silently binned. The mapping must stay total: a compiled unit with no assignment here is a hard compile error. Binning conventions applied (all reversible by editing this file): general multi-service ICUs (MICU, SICU) sit in Critical Care; service-aligned ICUs (HVICU, Neuro ICU, Transplant ICU) stay on their organ/service line — unit_type already carries the level of care, so lines slice by clinical service; vascular and cardiac surgery sit in Cardiac (Penn's Heart & Vascular umbrella); transplant sits in Surgery (no separate Transplant line in the starting set); neonatal intensive care sits in Women's Health & Neonatal, not Critical Care. EP-23 (2026-08-13): the owner ruled all 11 formerly-flagged units after a targeted OSINT session — end-states + evidence in each entry's note and in units.json; six units were retired to assets/data/archive/ep23_roster_rulings.json and their assignments removed here (same-commit, per the stale-assignment rule); gyn/gyn-onc joined Women's Health & Neonatal; the Oncology MICU follows the service-aligned-ICU convention into Oncology; MICU (Founders 8) and SICU (Rhoads 5) keep Critical Care populated.
